full_judgment: 21. The learned Advocate for the accused appellants submits that in this case the accused appellants were taken to police remand and from police remand they were produced before the Magistrate for recording their confessional statement and accordingly, their statements were recorded and, as such, the same cannot be considered as voluntary and true as the accused appellants were likely to make confessional statement out of fear. In support of his contention the learned Advocate relied upon the case of Nazrul Islam and others, vs State, reported in 45 DLR 142. He further submits that the Magistrate who recorded the statements of accused appellant Vim has not been examined in this case. He then submits that section 80 of the Evidence Act provides for making certain presumption in respect of a confession by an accused person produced before a Court, taken in accordance with law and reported to be signed by a Magistrate, In the case reported in 42 DLR (AD) 186 it was held that, it was at least injudicious to rely upon such confession without calling the Magistrate as a witness. The Court is required to see not only that the forms under section 164 and 264 Code of Criminal Procedure were complied with, but the substance underneath the law equally adhered to.
